scenes.heading: Functions and function notation
scenes.sub: One input in, exactly one output out
scenes.say: Almost every graph in senior maths is the graph of a function. Today you'll learn what makes something a function, and how to use f of x notation.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Press B4 on a vending machine: always the same snack
scenes.science: A function: each input x gives exactly one output y
scenes.breaks: A vending machine has a few buttons; f(x) = 2x + 1 accepts infinitely many inputs, even fractions.
scenes.say: Think of a vending machine. Press B four and you always get the same snack. Two buttons can give the same snack, and that's fine. But if B four sometimes gave chips and sometimes a drink, it wouldn't be a function.

scenes.heading: The vertical line test
notes: Parabola: cut once, so a function
Circle: cut twice, so not a function
scenes.say: Here's the vertical line test. First a parabola, then a circle. Now slide a vertical line across each one. It cuts the parabola only once, so that's a function. It cuts the circle twice, so one x-value has two y-values: not a function.
scenes.caption: The vertical line test. A vertical line cuts the parabola once, so it's a function. It cuts the circle twice, so one x-value has two y-values: not a function.

scenes.heading: Function notation
scenes.say: We write f of x equals two x plus one. f of three means put in three: two times three plus one is seven. So the point three, seven is on the graph. Solving f of x equals eleven means finding the input: x equals five.
scenes.caption: f(x) = 2x + 1. f(3) means put in 3: 2 × 3 + 1 = 7, so (3, 7) is on the graph. Solving f(x) = 11 means finding the input: x = 5.

scenes.heading: Substituting an expression
scenes.question: f(x) = x² − 1. Find f(x + 3).
scenes.say: f of x plus three means replace every x with x plus three, in brackets. Expand: x squared plus six x plus nine, minus one. That's x squared plus six x plus eight.
scenes.caption: f(x + 3): replace every x with (x + 3). Expand: x² + 6x + 9 − 1 = x² + 6x + 8.

scenes.heading: Domain vs range

right.title: Range
points: Read it up and down a graph

scenes.say: The domain is the set of inputs, the x-values. You can't square root a negative or divide by zero, so those restrict it. The range is the set of outputs, the y-values. D before R, x before y.

points: Function: one output for each input
scenes.say: Quick recap. A function gives one output for each input. Use the vertical line test on graphs. f of a means substitute; f of x equals b means solve. Domain is inputs, range is outputs. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. A function gives one output for each input. Use the vertical line test. f(a) means substitute; f(x) = b means solve. Domain is inputs, range is outputs. Now try the practice questions!
